subject: English
title: Arun and Maya's Night Time Discovery
hook: Arun and Maya explore the night sky and discover letters N to Z!

slides.title: Arun and Maya's Night Time Discovery
slides.inSimpleWords: Learn letters N to Z with two adventurous friends!

slides.title: N is for Nest and O is for Orange
slides.storyContext: Arun spots a bird's nest high in a tree. Maya picks an orange from a nearby bush.

points.label: Letter N
points.text: Nest starts with N

points.label: Letter O
points.text: Orange starts with O

slides.inSimpleWords: Two more letters as night begins to fall!

image.alt: N is for Nest and O is for Orange — Alphabet N to Z

slides.title: Understanding Letters N and O

points.label: Letter N
points.text: N is the 14th letter. It sounds like 'nnn' at the start of words.

points.label: Letter O
points.text: O is the 15th letter. It sounds like 'ohhh' — an open, round sound.

slides.inSimpleWords: N and O are two different letters with their own sounds!

slides.title: N and O Words

example.problem: What are some words that start with N and O?
example.solution: N words: nest, nose, name, number. O words: orange, owl, open, oven.

slides.inSimpleWords: Many words around us start with N and O!

slides.title: N and O Hunt

points.label: Challenge
points.text: Find one more N word and one more O word. Can you say them with Arun and Maya?

slides.inSimpleWords: Hunt for N and O words in your home!

slides.title: P is for Pig and Q is for Queen
slides.storyContext: They pass a sleeping pig in the farmyard. Maya pretends to be a queen with a crown!

points.label: Letter P
points.text: Pig starts with P

points.label: Letter Q
points.text: Queen starts with Q

slides.inSimpleWords: A pig and a queen show us two new letters!

image.alt: P is for Pig and Q is for Queen — Alphabet N to Z

slides.title: Understanding Letters P and Q

points.label: Letter P
points.text: P is the 16th letter. Sound: 'ppp' — lips come together and pop open.

points.label: Letter Q
points.text: Q is the 17th letter. Almost always followed by 'u' to make the 'qu' sound.

slides.inSimpleWords: P and Q are special — Q often brings U along!

slides.title: P and Q Words

example.problem: Can you think of P and Q words?
example.solution: P: pig, pen, pot, plant, play. Q: queen, quit, quilt, quarter.

slides.inSimpleWords: P and Q have many words we use!

slides.title: P and Q Challenge

points.label: Challenge
points.text: Find one more P word and one Q word. Remember, Q words almost always have 'u' after them!

slides.inSimpleWords: Can you find P and Q words in your books?

slides.title: R is for Rain and S is for Sun
slides.storyContext: Dark rain clouds gather, but they know tomorrow the sun will shine bright again.

points.label: Letter R
points.text: Rain starts with R

points.label: Letter S
points.text: Sun starts with S

slides.inSimpleWords: Rain and sun bring weather lessons today!

image.alt: R is for Rain and S is for Sun — Alphabet N to Z

slides.title: Understanding Letters R and S

points.label: Letter R
points.text: R is the 18th letter. Sound: 'rrr' — tongue curls slightly backward.

points.label: Letter S
points.text: S is the 19th letter. Sound: 'sss' — makes a soft hissing sound like a snake.

slides.inSimpleWords: R and S make very different sounds!

slides.title: R and S Words Around Us

example.problem: Are there R and S words in our homes and gardens?
example.solution: R: river, rose, rabbit, roof, run. S: star, seed, snake, stone, sit.

slides.inSimpleWords: Look around — R and S words are everywhere!

slides.title: R and S Hunt

points.label: Challenge
points.text: Say R words quickly: rabbit, rose, run, rain. Now S words: sun, star, sit, sand. Which sound do you like better?

slides.inSimpleWords: Practice the R and S sounds with Arun and Maya!

slides.title: T is for Tiger and U is for Umbrella
slides.storyContext: They see a painting of a tiger in a cave. Maya carries an umbrella to stay dry.

points.label: Letter T
points.text: Tiger starts with T

points.label: Letter U
points.text: Umbrella starts with U

slides.inSimpleWords: A tiger and umbrella teach two new sounds!

image.alt: T is for Tiger and U is for Umbrella — Alphabet N to Z

slides.title: Understanding Letters T and U

points.label: Letter T
points.text: T is the 20th letter. Sound: 'ttt' — tip of tongue touches top teeth.

points.label: Letter U
points.text: U is the 21st letter. Sound: 'uh' — one of our vowel sounds with rounded lips.

slides.inSimpleWords: T is a consonant and U is a vowel!

slides.title: T and U Words

example.problem: What T and U words can you name?
example.solution: T: tiger, tree, toy, table, talk. U: umbrella, under, up, urn, uncle.

slides.inSimpleWords: T and U words help us talk about many things!

slides.title: T and U Say-Along

points.label: Challenge
points.text: Say these sentences: 'Tiger talks to turtle.' 'Uncle uses umbrella under tree.' Notice the T and U sounds!

slides.inSimpleWords: Practice saying T and U words in sentences!

slides.title: V is for Violin and W is for Water
slides.storyContext: Arun hears a beautiful violin playing. Maya splashes in water nearby.

points.label: Letter V
points.text: Violin starts with V

points.label: Letter W
points.text: Water starts with W

slides.inSimpleWords: Music and water show us two more letters!

image.alt: V is for Violin and W is for Water — Alphabet N to Z

slides.title: Understanding Letters V and W

points.label: Letter V
points.text: V is the 22nd letter. Sound: 'vvv' — bottom lip touches top teeth gently.

points.label: Letter W
points.text: W is the 23rd letter. Sound: 'www' — like blowing a gentle breeze or making your lips round.

slides.inSimpleWords: V and W are consonants with smooth sounds!

slides.title: V and W Words

example.problem: Can you think of V and W words?
example.solution: V: vest, vine, voice, violin, victory. W: window, walk, wave, wish, water.

slides.inSimpleWords: Many common words start with V and W!

slides.title: V and W Exploration

points.label: Challenge
points.text: Find one V word and one W word. Say them slowly to notice how V and W sound different!

slides.inSimpleWords: Hunt for more V and W words!

slides.title: X is for Xylophone
slides.storyContext: They hear a child playing a colorful xylophone in the village square!

points.label: Letter X
points.text: Xylophone starts with X

slides.inSimpleWords: Xylophone makes a musical letter sound!

image.alt: X is for Xylophone — Alphabet N to Z

slides.title: Understanding Letter X

points.label: Letter X
points.text: X is the 24th letter. It's the rarest letter in English!

points.label: X Sounds
points.text: At the start: 'z' sound (xylophone, x-ray). In the middle: 'ks' sound (box, six, mix).

slides.inSimpleWords: X is special because it's so rare!

slides.title: X Words Are Rare

example.problem: Why are X words so hard to find?
example.solution: X is the rarest letter! Examples: xylophone, x-ray, box, six, mix, fix.

slides.inSimpleWords: X words are like treasure — hard to find!

slides.title: X Word Challenge

points.label: Challenge
points.text: Find one word with X in the middle (like box or six). Then find one with X at the start!

slides.inSimpleWords: Can you find more rare X words?

slides.title: Y is for Yak and Z is for Zoo
slides.storyContext: In a book, Arun sees a yak. Maya dreams of visiting a zoo full of animals.

points.label: Letter Y
points.text: Yak starts with Y

points.label: Letter Z
points.text: Zoo starts with Z

slides.inSimpleWords: A yak and zoo finish all 26 letters!

image.alt: Y is for Yak and Z is for Zoo — Alphabet N to Z

slides.title: Understanding Letters Y and Z

points.label: Letter Y
points.text: Y is the 25th letter. Can be a vowel (gym, my, happy) or consonant (yes, yak).

points.label: Letter Z
points.text: Z is the 26th and final letter! Sound: 'zzz' — like a buzzing bee.

slides.inSimpleWords: Y and Z complete the whole alphabet!

slides.title: Y and Z Words

example.problem: What Y and Z words do you know?
example.solution: Y: yellow, year, yarn, yoga, yes. Z: zebra, zero, zone, zoom, zigzag.

slides.inSimpleWords: Y and Z words are fun to practice!

slides.title: Complete the Alphabet

points.label: Challenge
points.text: Say the full alphabet N-Z quickly three times! Can you go faster each time?

slides.inSimpleWords: You're an alphabet master now!

slides.title: N to Z Complete!
slides.storyContext: Arun and Maya write all 26 letters on the ground under the stars.

points.label: Full Alphabet
points.text: N O P Q R S T U V W X Y Z — completed!

slides.inSimpleWords: All 26 letters learned! You are an alphabet champion!

image.alt: N to Z Complete! — Alphabet N to Z

subject: English
title: Arun and Maya's Sound Adventure
hook: Listen and learn as Arun and Maya discover the magic of vowel and consonant sounds!

slides.title: Arun and Maya's Sound Adventure
slides.inSimpleWords: Discover vowels and consonants together!

slides.title: A is for Vowel
slides.storyContext: Arun opens his mouth wide and says 'Ahhh' like at the doctor's office!

points.label: Vowel A
points.text: Five special letters called vowels: A E I O U

slides.inSimpleWords: A is a special vowel sound we can sing!

image.alt: A is for Vowel — Vowels and Consonants

slides.title: What is a Vowel?

points.label: Vowels
points.text: Vowels are special letters: A, E, I, O, U. Your mouth stays open when you say them.

points.label: Vowel Sound A
points.text: Say 'ahhh' — feel how your mouth is wide open!

slides.inSimpleWords: Vowels let air flow freely through your mouth!

slides.title: Words with Vowel A

example.problem: Where can we find the vowel A in words?
example.solution: Apple, ant, and, ask, art, animal — all have the vowel A!

slides.inSimpleWords: A appears in so many words!

slides.title: Find More A Words

points.label: Challenge
points.text: Find three words with vowel A. Say them aloud with Arun and Maya!

slides.inSimpleWords: Hunt for A words around you!

slides.title: E and I are Vowels Too
slides.storyContext: Maya says 'Eee' like she sees something. Arun says 'Iiii' like a mouse squeaking!

points.label: Vowel E
points.text: E makes a long 'eee' sound

points.label: Vowel I
points.text: I makes a high 'iii' sound

slides.inSimpleWords: E and I are vowels that sound different!

image.alt: E and I are Vowels Too — Vowels and Consonants

slides.title: Understanding E and I

points.label: Vowel E
points.text: E sounds like 'eee' — your lips stretch a bit when you say it.

points.label: Vowel I
points.text: I sounds like 'iii' — a high, thin sound like a squeak!

slides.inSimpleWords: E and I are two very different vowel sounds!

slides.title: E and I Word Search

example.problem: Can we find E and I words?
example.solution: E: egg, elephant, end, eye, ear. I: ice, ink, igloo, ill.

slides.inSimpleWords: Many words have E and I in them!

slides.title: E and I Say-Along

points.label: Challenge
points.text: Say these: 'Elephant eats eggs.' 'Ice is icy.' Notice the E and I sounds!

slides.inSimpleWords: Practice saying E and I words together!

slides.title: O and U Complete Vowels
slides.storyContext: Arun says 'Ohhh' when he sees the moon. Maya says 'Uhhh' when confused!

points.label: Vowel O
points.text: O makes a round 'ohhh' sound

points.label: Vowel U
points.text: U makes a deep 'uh' sound

slides.inSimpleWords: O and U are the last two vowel sounds!

image.alt: O and U Complete Vowels — Vowels and Consonants

slides.title: Understanding O and U

points.label: Vowel O
points.text: O sounds like 'ohhh' — your lips form a circle! Say 'oh' like amazed.

points.label: Vowel U
points.text: U sounds like 'uh' — deep and dark. Say 'up' with your mouth rounded.

slides.inSimpleWords: O and U complete the five vowel sounds!

slides.title: O and U Words

example.problem: What O and U words can we find?
example.solution: O: orange, open, oven, ocean, only. U: up, use, under, umbrella, uncle.

slides.inSimpleWords: O and U words are all around us!

slides.title: O and U Hunt

points.label: Challenge
points.text: Find two O words and two U words. Can you say them in sentences?

slides.inSimpleWords: Search for O and U words!

slides.title: Five Vowels Together
slides.storyContext: Arun and Maya sit in a circle and sing all five vowel sounds together!

points.label: All Vowels
points.text: A E I O U — the five magic vowels

slides.inSimpleWords: A E I O U are the five vowel letters!

image.alt: Five Vowels Together — Vowels and Consonants

slides.title: Vowel Singing Challenge

points.label: Challenge
points.text: Say the vowels in order: A E I O U. Can you sing them like a song?

slides.inSimpleWords: Vowels are fun to sing!

slides.title: B is for Consonant
slides.storyContext: Arun says 'Bbb' and his lips vibrate. These sounds need vowels to be heard clearly!

points.label: Consonant B
points.text: Most other letters are consonants

slides.inSimpleWords: B is a consonant that needs a vowel helper!

image.alt: B is for Consonant — Vowels and Consonants

slides.title: What is a Consonant?

points.label: Consonants
points.text: Consonants are all the other letters. Your mouth blocks air partly when you say them.

points.label: Consonant B
points.text: B needs to stop the air with your lips — 'bbb' by itself is hard to hear!

slides.inSimpleWords: Consonants need vowels to make clear sounds!

slides.title: B Words

example.problem: Why does B sound strange all by itself?
example.solution: B alone = 'bbb'. With vowels: ba, be, bi, bo, bu. Much clearer!

slides.inSimpleWords: Adding vowels to B makes real words!

slides.title: More Consonants
slides.storyContext: Maya lists consonants: C, D, F, G, H... Arun makes all their sounds with her!

points.label: More Consonants
points.text: C D F G H J K L M N P R S T V W X Y Z

slides.inSimpleWords: Consonants are all the other letter sounds!

image.alt: More Consonants — Vowels and Consonants

slides.title: 21 Consonants

points.label: Consonants Count
points.text: 21 consonants: B C D F G H J K L M N P R S T V W X Y Z

points.label: Pattern
points.text: 5 vowels + 21 consonants = 26 letters of the alphabet!

slides.inSimpleWords: Most letters are consonants, not vowels!

slides.title: Consonant + Vowel = Word
slides.storyContext: Arun says 'B' + 'A' = 'BA'. Maya says 'C' + 'A' = 'CA'. Together they make words!

example.problem: B alone sounds 'bbb' but we cannot hear it clearly
example.solution: B + A = 'BA' — now it's a clear sound!

slides.inSimpleWords: Consonants and vowels work together to make words!

image.alt: Consonant + Vowel = Word — Vowels and Consonants

slides.title: Make Your Own Words

points.label: Challenge
points.text: Pick a consonant (like D) and add each vowel: DA, DE, DI, DO, DU. Can you make more?

slides.inSimpleWords: You can create simple words with consonant + vowel!

slides.title: Vowel Combinations
slides.inSimpleWords: Short vowel sounds are the most basic sounds!

points.text: Short vowel sounds: a (cat), e (egg), i (ink), o (on), u (up)
points.label: Short Vowels

points.text: These five sounds are the foundation of English!
points.label: Same But Different

slides.title: Short Vowel Word Practice
slides.inSimpleWords: Practice short vowel sounds in real sentences!

example.solution: A cat sat on a big log. I can see an ant in the box.
example.problem: Can we find short vowel words in sentences?

slides.title: Vowel Challenge
slides.inSimpleWords: Can you use all five vowels in one sentence?

points.text: Make a sentence using A, E, I, O, U � one of each! 'A ant eats ice on unique days.'
points.label: Challenge

slides.title: Vowels and Consonants
slides.storyContext: Under the banyan tree, Arun and Maya write vowels in red and consonants in blue!

points.label: 5 Vowels
points.text: A E I O U

points.label: 21 Consonants
points.text: All the other letters

slides.inSimpleWords: Five vowels and many consonants make all words!

image.alt: Vowels and Consonants — Vowels and Consonants

subject: English
title: Arun and Maya Make Sentences
hook: Watch Arun and Maya build their first sentences together!

slides.title: Arun and Maya Make Sentences
slides.inSimpleWords: Learn how to build sentences that make sense!

slides.title: What is a Sentence?
slides.storyContext: Arun says 'I like milk.' Maya says 'I like honey.' These are sentences!

points.label: Sentence
points.text: A sentence tells us a complete idea

slides.inSimpleWords: A sentence is words that tell us something!

image.alt: What is a Sentence? — Simple Sentences

slides.title: Understanding Sentences

points.label: Definition
points.text: A sentence is a group of words that expresses a complete thought.

points.label: Complete Idea
points.text: Everyone who reads it must understand what you mean.

slides.inSimpleWords: Sentences help us share our thoughts with others!

slides.title: Sentence vs. Not a Sentence

example.problem: Is 'very fast' a sentence or not?
example.solution: 'Very fast' is just words. But 'The car is very fast' is a complete sentence!

slides.inSimpleWords: A sentence needs to tell a complete idea!

slides.title: Identify Complete Sentences

points.label: Challenge
points.text: Is 'running fast' a sentence? What about 'Arun runs fast'? Can you tell the difference?

slides.inSimpleWords: Some are complete sentences, some are not!

slides.title: Sentences Need Words in Order
slides.storyContext: Maya says 'The cat sat.' Arun tries to say 'Sat the cat.' It sounds funny!

points.label: Word Order
points.text: Words in a sentence must be in the right order

slides.inSimpleWords: Words must go in the right order to make sense!

image.alt: Sentences Need Words in Order — Simple Sentences

slides.title: The Importance of Order

points.label: Example 1
points.text: 'Dog chased ball' vs. 'Ball chased dog' — very different meanings!

points.label: Example 2
points.text: 'Girl ran home' vs. 'Home ran girl' — only one makes sense!

slides.inSimpleWords: Word order changes the meaning of a sentence!

slides.title: Word Order Matters

example.solution: 'Tiger chased Arun' vs. 'Arun chased tiger' — completely different stories!

slides.inSimpleWords: The same words in different orders mean different things!

slides.title: Fix the Word Order

points.label: Challenge
points.text: Rearrange these: 'eats rice girl' — make it a proper sentence order! What about 'plays Arun'?

slides.inSimpleWords: Can you fix the jumbled words?

slides.title: Who and What - Subject and Action
slides.storyContext: Arun says 'The boy runs.' 'The boy' is WHO, 'runs' is the ACTION.

points.label: Subject
points.text: 'The boy' tells us WHO

points.label: Action
points.text: 'runs' tells us WHAT they do

slides.inSimpleWords: Every sentence needs a WHO and a WHAT happens!

image.alt: Who and What - Subject and Action — Simple Sentences

slides.title: Subject and Verb

points.label: Subject
points.text: The subject is WHO or WHAT the sentence is about. Example: 'The cat', 'Maya', 'The ball'

points.label: Verb (Action)
points.text: The verb tells us the ACTION. Example: 'runs', 'sits', 'jumps', 'eats'

slides.inSimpleWords: Subject = WHO or WHAT. Verb = the ACTION!

slides.title: Subject and Verb in Sentences

example.problem: What are the subject and verb in 'The bird flies'?

slides.inSimpleWords: Find the subject and verb in every sentence!

slides.title: Identify Subjects and Verbs

points.label: Challenge
points.text: Find the subject and verb: 'Arun plays football.' Can you find two more sentences and identify them?

slides.inSimpleWords: Practice finding subjects and verbs!

slides.title: Simple Sentence Pattern
slides.storyContext: Maya teaches: Subject + Verb = Simple Sentence. She writes on the sand.

points.label: Pattern
points.text: WHO (subject) + DOES WHAT (verb) = sentence

slides.inSimpleWords: Subject and verb together make a complete sentence!

image.alt: Simple Sentence Pattern — Simple Sentences

slides.title: Making Sentences
slides.storyContext: Arun and Maya practice together. Arun says a subject, Maya adds the action.

example.problem: I have words: 'dog', 'runs', 'the' — can we make a sentence?

slides.inSimpleWords: Subject + Verb = A sentence that makes sense!

image.alt: Making Sentences — Simple Sentences

slides.title: Naming the Subject

points.label: Proper Subjects
points.text: Subjects can be: people (Arun, Maya), animals (cat, dog), or things (book, table).

points.label: With 'The'
points.text: We often add 'The' before the subject: 'The dog', 'The girl', 'The bird'.

slides.inSimpleWords: Subjects tell us what the sentence is about!

slides.title: Create Your Own Subjects

points.label: Challenge
points.text: Think of a subject (like 'The monkey'). Now add action verbs: jumps, plays, swings. Make sentences!

slides.inSimpleWords: You can make many sentences with one subject!

slides.title: More Simple Sentences
slides.storyContext: Arun says 'The girl eats rice.' Maya says 'The bird flies high.' Both are perfect sentences!

points.label: Sentence 1
points.text: The girl eats rice.

points.label: Sentence 2
points.text: The bird flies high.

slides.inSimpleWords: Practice making more sentences with your own ideas!

image.alt: More Simple Sentences — Simple Sentences

slides.title: Different Sentence Actions

points.label: Action Verbs
points.text: Verbs describe actions: eat, play, run, jump, swim, read, write, sing, dance

points.label: State Verbs
points.text: Some verbs describe state: is, are, has, have, like, want

slides.inSimpleWords: Verbs are words that describe doing or being!

slides.title: Verbs in Sentences

example.problem: What are some verbs Arun and Maya can use?
example.solution: eat, play, run, sit, read, write, dance, laugh, help, teach

slides.inSimpleWords: Many action words become great verbs!

slides.title: Create Verb Sentences

points.label: Challenge
points.text: Pick three verbs (like jump, sing, paint). Make sentences with them: 'Maya jumps.', 'Arun sings.'

slides.inSimpleWords: Different verbs create different sentences!

slides.title: Sentences Must End with a Period
slides.storyContext: Arun says 'I see a butterfly' but forgets the period. Maya adds a dot at the end!

points.label: Period (.)
points.text: Every sentence ends with a period (.)

slides.inSimpleWords: Always put a period at the end of a sentence!

image.alt: Sentences Must End with a Period — Simple Sentences

slides.title: Punctuation Rules

points.label: Period (.)
points.text: Marks the end of a statement or thought.

points.label: Capital Letter
points.text: The first word of a sentence starts with a CAPITAL letter.

slides.inSimpleWords: Periods and capital letters make sentences complete!

slides.title: Proper Sentence Format

example.solution: 'The cat sits.' — Capital T at start, period at end!

slides.inSimpleWords: Always start with a capital letter and end with a period!

slides.title: Fix the Sentences

points.label: Challenge
points.text: Fix these: 'the dog runs' and 'maya plays' — add capital letters and periods! Try three more.

slides.inSimpleWords: Can you fix sentences with proper punctuation?

slides.title: Sentences Are Complete Thoughts
slides.storyContext: Arun and Maya write three sentences about their day on the wall!

points.label: Sentence 1
points.text: The sun shines brightly.

points.label: Sentence 2
points.text: We play in the garden.

points.label: Sentence 3
points.text: The wind blows gently.

slides.inSimpleWords: A sentence = WHO + DOES WHAT + period (.)!

image.alt: Sentences Are Complete Thoughts — Simple Sentences
